english.title: Detainee / person charged fail / refuse to provide a sample for Class 'A' drug test
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person in police detention

(A)_[arrested for and at the time the requirement was made had not been charged with]_
(B)_[charged with]_

(C)_[an offence, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFENCE..), contained within Schedule 6 to the Criminal Justice and Court Services Act 2000,]_
(D)_[an offence, namely **(..SPECIFY..), and a police inspector has authorised the taking of a sample,]_

failed without good cause to provide a

(E)_[sample of urine]_
(F)_[non intimate sample]_

for the purpose of ascertaining whether you had a Class 'A' drug specified in Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 in your body
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 63B(8) and 63C(1) of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Samples may be taken from a detained person who has attained the age of 14 years and who is charged with either a 'trigger offence' or charged with any offence where an authority for the taking has been given by an officer of the rank of inspector or above. (NOTE: The taking of samples from person aged 14 to 17 years is only available in pilot area - consult your Forces policy).
(ii) Where the arrest condition only has been met samples may be taken from a detained person who has attained the age of 18 years.
(iii) Other conditions must also be met before a request for a sample may be made.
(iv) The sample may only be taken by a specified person.
(v) See Section 65 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 for the meaning of "non intimate sample"
(vi) Section 63 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 has been amended by Section 57 of the Criminal Justice and Court Services Act 2000. In addition option "B" in relation to the provision of a sample by a person arrested but not charged was inserted into section 63 by section 7 of the Drugs Act 2005.
